objective: pack two independent 64-byte destination descriptors into one aligned 128-byte issue packet to reduce command/state admission stalls without changing source arithmetic, parent semantics, fusion capacity or vector storage

packet_contract.descriptor_identity_and_order: every canonical M53/M89 descriptor is preserved exactly once; issue width changes only the number of ready descriptors accepted in one cycle
packet_contract.partial_packet_rule: one valid descriptor may issue alone without creating a synthetic destination
packet_contract.ready_rule: a descriptor may occupy a packet lane only at or after its unchanged ready_since cycle
packet_contract.calendar_rule: an issue cycle accepts at most width descriptors; command completion remains one cycle after issue
unchanged_resources: K6 fusion engine and source-bank schedule

width4_policy.otherwise: kill width4 and retain width2 as the only candidate

kill_conditions: width1 fails exact M89 K6 reproduction
width2 fails any arithmetic, dependency, descriptor, occupancy, source, p95 or per-sample gate
width2 aggregate integrated improvement is below 0.5 percent
width4 is promoted for less than 0.5 percent incremental integrated improvement versus width2
any result depends on changing parent choice, fusion fanout, FIFO depth or vector payload capacity beyond the coupled timing consequences of descriptor issue width

admitted_after_validation: exact frozen-cohort transaction-model comparison against M89 K6
descriptor issue-packet opportunity and width2/width4 cycle sensitivity
forbidden: RTL correctness, 128/256-byte command-path timing feasibility or synthesized PPA
equal-area, accuracy, full-network, system, DATE headline or best-paper claim
